page: Microsoft Azure B2pls_v2 is a burstable virtual machine belonging to the Bpsv2 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an ARM64 architecture powered by an Ampere Altra ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor operating at 3.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 2 physical cores, 2 vCPUs, and 1.0 thread per core. It is equipped with 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding 2.0 GB of RAM per core. The processor features 64 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It supports AES cryptography but lacks AVX, AMX, and virtualization flags. There is no local storage bundled with this instance, though it is premium storage capable, and it includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data reveals that the B2pls_v2 exhibits modest performance characteristics. In single-core CPU testing via stress-ng, it achieves an average score of 1821.89, while its multi-core CPU score of 3614.38 is categorized as weak. Memory bandwidth tests show a poor read-only small block cached speed of 140.82 GB/sec, alongside weak uncached large block read and write speeds of 27.02 GB/sec and 16.61 GB/sec, respectively. Under Geekbench, the server registers a weak single-core score of 1111.0 and a poor multi-core score of 2010.0. Cryptographic and physics performance are also limited, with a Passmark CPU encryption score of 321.76 and a physics score of 370.75, both falling into the poor category.

Given its burstable CPU allocation and low memory capacity, the B2pls_v2 is positioned as a highly cost-efficient option for workloads with variable CPU utilization. It is suited for lightweight tasks such as static web serving, where it achieves a throughput of 2.88 GB/sec, or basic database operations, registering 2.78 million Redis SET operations per second. However, its low memory bandwidth and poor multi-threaded decompression performance make it unsuitable for memory-intensive applications, large-scale data processing, or complex LLM inference.
